A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Veludharan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogeshwari Caves hewed during 6th century CE, is one of the finest specimen of Brahmanical rock-cut architecture and bears similarity with Elephanta (Cave no.1) and Dhumar lena (Cave no. 29) at Ellora. On plan, it consists of agra mandapa, mukha mandapa and garbhagriha. Vakataka and later Vakataka, influence can clearly be noticed in its architectural planning and sculptural execution. Some scholars believe that the caves were excavated under the patronage of Maurya of Konkan, Kalachuri (Traikutakas). Jogeshwari cave is adorned with a few beautiful sculptural representations of Lakulisa. Kalyansundarmurti, Shiv Parvati playing dyuta, Natraja, Ravananugraha, Makartornas, ayudhprushas, Dwarapalas etc.
It was declared as a protected monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India, vide gazette notification no. 2704A, dated 26.05. 1009

featured_reviews.name: Vaibhav Gajur
featured_reviews.review_text:
A visit to the Jogeshwari Caves offers a fascinating glimpse into Mumbai's deep historical roots, dating all the way back to 560 CE. If you are a history or archaeology enthusiast, set aside 1–2 hours to explore this ancient site.
Key Highlights & What to Expect
Ancient Heritage: The sheer age of these caves is awe-inspiring. They hold immense historical value as one of the oldest surviving rock-cut Hindu temple caves in the city.
Weathered Carvings: Be prepared that many of the old carvings are heavily weathered. While their original splendor may be diminished, they still tell a story of a distant past.
Unique Temple Setup: The main sanctum is a must-see. The temple dedicated to Goddess Jogeshwari Mata is located in the basement. You will also find shrines for Lord Shiva in one corner and a more hidden shrine for Lord Hanuman in another.
East Gate Temple: If you enter or exit via the East Gate, you'll find a separate temple dedicated to Lord Ganesh.
Multiple Entrances: The caves are accessible via two main entrances, one on the East and one on the West.
📸 Pro-Tip: The Hidden Viewpoint
After exploring the basement shrine, make sure to ask a local for the way to the top of the caves. The journey offers a reward: a good panoramic view of the entire structure and surrounding area.
🕉️ Other Shrines Nearby
The complex holds several other important deities worth visiting:
There is a second dedicated temple to Lord Hanuman (ask a local for directions, as it might be slightly hidden).
Look for a temple housing Kal Bhairav and other deities on the other side of the complex.
⏱️ Essential Visiting Hours
Please note the specific timings for your visit:
The temple is closed during the afternoon.
It reopens in the evening at 4 PM.
Recommendation: Visit in the early morning or late evening to experience the temple and avoid the mid-day closure.
Overall: Jogeshwari Caves is a unique, spiritual, and historical experience. While the carvings are worn, the atmosphere and the ancient rock-cut architecture make this a worthwhile stop for anyone interested in Mumbai's pre-medieval history.

featured_reviews.name: Suresh Isave
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves feature beautiful carvings, though some aspects appear unfinished.  There's a large cave with the Jogeshwari Devi temple, and grand pillars are present.  However, the area doesn't seem well-maintained, and there's a noticeable unpleasant smell from plastic waste.  Parking is also an issue, as none is available close by. Entry is free.

featured_reviews.name: Kunal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: The Jogeshwari Caves act as a haunting reminder of Mumbai's deep ancient roots, representing some of the earliest and most significant Hindu and Buddhist rock-cut architecture in the region. Stepping inside, one can still sense the majesty of the past through the massive pillars and the lingering spiritual aura of the central Shiva shrine. However, the site is in a heartbreaking state of decay, suffocated by encroaching slums and plagued by sewage seepage and piled-up debris that obscure its historical value. It is a heritage monument that is desperately crying out for comprehensive restoration and protection; without immediate intervention to clear the surroundings and preserve the crumbling rockwork, this archaeological treasure risks being lost entirely to urban neglect.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
The caves are located just off the Western Express Highway and are surrounded by heavy encroachments. Access is through a long flight of stairs that leads into the main hall of the cavern. Unfortunately, the site is in very poor condition—extremely unhygienic, poorly maintained, and the area smells terrible.

I would strongly advise against making a special trip, as you are likely to feel disappointed and even upset by the neglect and lack of care shown by the authorities and local people. The site remains open at all times with no entry gate or time restrictions, which further contributes to its deteriorated state.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Jogeshwari Caves and it was a surprisingly powerful experience. One of the oldest rock-cut cave temples in India, the place has a raw, ancient energy that you can actually feel as you walk inside. The carvings dedicated to Lord Shiva, especially forms like Nataraja, are beautiful and carry a quiet intensity.

The caves are not very well maintained compared to places like Elephanta Caves, and there can be waterlogging and a bit of mess around, but that also adds to the untouched, authentic feel of the site.

If you enjoy history, architecture, or just want a peaceful spot away from the usual crowds, this place is worth a visit. A hidden gem in Mumbai that deserves more care and attention.

description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. featured_reviews.name: Ritesh K R
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kondivite Caves (Mahakali Caves) are one of Mumbai’s most underrated historical gems—quiet, raw, and deeply rooted in India’s ancient Buddhist past.

Dating back to around the 2nd century BCE, these rock-cut caves began in the Hinayana tradition and later saw influences of the Mahayana phase, remaining active up to around the 6th century CE and even beyond till the 12th century in some form. You can actually sense this long continuity as you walk through the caves—simple early structures evolving into more developed spaces.

Carved out of basalt rock and once surrounded by dense forests, the setting would have been ideal for monks—isolated, peaceful, and close to natural water sources. Like Bhaje and Karle caves, the site reflects how geography and trade routes shaped spiritual centres.

The presence of Pali inscriptions adds another layer of authenticity and historical depth, connecting you directly to the lives and practices of the monks who once lived here.

Today, the caves still carry a quiet, meditative energy, though the surroundings could definitely be cleaner and better maintained. More signage or guided interpretation would really help visitors appreciate the historical context.

Overall, a fascinating visit—especially if you enjoy history, archaeology, or simply discovering hidden layers of Mumbai beyond its modern chaos.

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Thigale
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Mahakali Caves (historically known as the Kondivite Caves) are a hidden archaeological treasure tucked away in the bustle of Andheri East, Mumbai.
​Whether you're a history buff or just looking for a pocket of peace in the city, here is a review of this ancient site.
​The Experience: A Step Back in Time
​The Mahakali Caves are a group of 19 rock-cut Buddhist monuments dating from the 1st Century BCE to the 6th Century CE. Carved directly into solid black basalt rock, these caves served as a quiet retreat for Buddhist monks long before Mumbai became a financial hub.
​The Architecture
​Cave 9 (The Main Attraction): This is the largest and most significant cave. It features a Chaitya (prayer hall) with a stupa and a unique semicircular wall. Look closely at the walls—even though they have weathered over 2,000 years, you can still see mutilated figures of Buddha and characters from Buddhist mythology.
​The Viharas: The other caves are mostly Viharas (monasteries). These are small, stark cells where monks lived and meditated. Their simplicity is a powerful contrast to the modern skyscrapers visible in the distance.
​The View: Located on a small hill, the site offers a panoramic view of the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR). It’s a surreal experience to stand in a 2,000-year-old monastery while watching the "maximum city" rush by below.

Excellant place for Morning Walker, kids and families.

HERITAGE GARDEN: De-stressing and Rejuvenating in a Different World

Pramod Chavan

Surrounded by high-rise concrete buildings and glass-fronted skyscrapers opposite the Glen Towers on Cliff Avenue Road in Powai, a Heritage Garden means Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee Udyan is a de-stressing and rejuvenating world.

The special thing about this ten-acre park is that it is not just a park for one class or one age group. On one side are college students on the fence and on the other a group of senior citizens reminiscing. Here, among the youth the guitar tunes, and among the senior citizens, someone easily makes the flute tunes, mesmerizing the entire atmosphere.

Apart from the magnificence of the surrounding residential complexes, it is the right space for yoga enthusiasts with its many offices and commercial setups. It has become a place for those who practice regular and mixed martial arts.

The landscaped lawns, a separate play area for children, a Japanese-style Miyawaki patch on one side and a circular walking path that winds around the periphery of the park make the Heritage Garden a pleasant place to spend an evening with your loved ones.

Heritage Garden is one of the main places for morning walkers in Powai and the surrounding area. There is a beautiful gazebo apart from benches at regular intervals. It also has a beautiful artificial pond which often has beautiful lotus flowers.

The stone structure along the circular walkway attracts the attention of all new visitors. There is also a restroom on one side of the park.

Another special feature of this park is that some other parks in the city often organize events, so people coming to the park have a lot of trouble. However, events or other mass activities are still not allowed here without permission.

The man-made wells located at the corners of the park are used the most during monsoons. But it has not been able to escape from the habit of people coming to the garden to throw large amounts of waste.

Garden gates open at 5 am, after that they are closed from 12 noon to 4.30 pm... and open again from 4.30 pm to 10 pm.

Forest Park in Powai is an escape from the pollution and the hustle of the city. Here’s why you should take some time off.
